notes: Net map (16 nets, 24 components, all traced from the ink; drawing is rotated ~90 deg so every BJT bar is horizontal or near-horizontal). 0 = the long LEFT RAIL, x~69 at the top sloping to x~90 at the bottom, terminated by GND 14 at (65,429); it only crosses the R9 column at (274,344), it does not join it. n13 = anode (right) of Diode 0 -> right to (334,330) -> down x~335 to the base bar of BJT-NPN 4. n14 = '+5V' node at the filled dot (277,414): bottom of R9 + emitter of BJT 4 (from the right) + the horizontal left to the dot (219,419) which carries the collector of BJT 8 and the emitter of BJT-PNP 6 + V-DC 22 (+5V) hanging below at (282,472). n15 = collector (down-left lead) of BJT-PNP 6 -> left along y~390 -> down x~131 to the base bar of BJT-NPN 8. Judgment calls: (a) TWO 4-way crossings are drawn as a shallow 'V' notch in the horizontal wire with NO dot: (124,274) [GND-rail-to-R17-left horizontal vs the n9 column] and (274,344) [the n12 diode link vs the R9 column]. Elsewhere this drafter marks every real junction with an unmistakable filled blob or drawn ring - e.g. (277,414), (262,204), (331,103), (219,419), (181,344), (167,8) - all checked at 14x. So the V-notch is this drafter's crossover glyph and both were read as CROSSINGS, not junctions. (124,274) also has to be a crossing electrically: joining it would tie the base of BJT 11 to its own grounded emitter and short the +3V source 23 to ground through R17. (b) Consequently Diodes 1 and 0 form a series pair pointing from the base of BJT 4 (n13, anode of D0) through n12 to the base of BJT 6 / collector of BJT 11 (n11, cathode of D1) - a level-shift chain. (c) BJT 2 (PNP) symbol read with a horizontal base bar at y~219 spanning x 231-243: base lead is the vertical dropping to the +3V node, the up-right lead carrying the arrowhead is the emitter (to +6V) and the up-left diagonal to (215,206) is the collector. This reading is the one whose extent matches the published bbox centre (229.0,211.7). (d) PNP/NPN lead assignment everywhere from the arrowhead: on 3, 7, 6 and 2 the arrow sits on the lead pointing back toward the bar (PNP emitter); on 12, 15, 11, 8 and 4 the arrow points away from the bar (NPN emitter). Emitters of NPN 12, 15, 11 and 8 all land on the ground rail; only BJT 4's emitter goes to n14. (e) Diode orientation: both diodes are drawn with the bar (cathode) on the LEFT and the triangle back (anode) on the RIGHT; terminal index 0 is the cathode side, index 1 the anode side (2-terminal order does not affect any metric). (f) All six V-DC (one port) arrows are supply stubs (+3V, +3V, +5V, +6V, +10V, +15V) and each was paired with the node its stub is drawn onto. No component lies outside the 512x512 crop. (g) n8 (bases of 12 and 15 tied, both emitters grounded, no other connection) is electrically inert but is exactly what the ink shows - the vertical between the two base bars is clean and unbranched at 10x.
